style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A psalm that starts with the whole earth and ends with one man's testimony. Shout to God, all the earth; say to Him, how awesome are Your works -- come and see them: He turned the sea into dry land, they crossed the river on foot. Then the nation's own story, the exodus pattern applied to a recent rescue: You tested us, refined us like silver, brought us into the net, laid a heavy load on our hips, let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and water -- and You brought us out into a place of overflow. So the psalmist goes into the house with burnt offerings to pay the vows his lips made when he was in trouble, and then he turns to the congregation: come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell what He has done for my soul. The confession at the heart of it is the verse every praying person has had to face: if I had looked with favor on iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened -- but He did listen. Blessed be God, who did not turn away my prayer, or His covenant love from me.

1.text: For the choir director. A song, a psalm. Raise a shout to God, all the earth!
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Song [shir] or Psalm [mizmor]. Make a joyful noise [rua -- shout] unto God [Elohim], all ye lands ['all the earth', eretz, the KJV margin]:
1.notes: hariu l-Elohim kol-ha-aretz (H7321, H430, H776): the margin has it -- ALL THE EARTH, not 'lands' -- told to raise the war-shout of Psalm 100:1. The psalm opens as wide as it can and will narrow, verse by verse, to one man's soul.

2.text: Make music to the glory of His name; make His praise glorious.
2.amp: Sing forth [zamar] the honour [kabod -- glory] of His name [shem]: make [sum] His praise [tehillah] glorious [kabod].
2.notes: zammeru khebod-shemo (H2167, H3519, H8034): play the glory of His Name -- simu khabod tehillato (H7760, H3519, H8416): SET glory as His praise -- kabod twice: the weight of the Name, and the weight the praise should carry to match it.

3.text: Say to God, 'How awesome are Your works! Through the greatness of Your power Your enemies come cringing to You.'
3.amp: Say [amar] unto God [Elohim], How terrible [yare -- awesome] are You in Your works [maaseh]! through the greatness [rob] of Your power [oz] shall Your enemies [oyeb] submit ['yield feigned obedience: Heb. lie', kachash -- cringe, the KJV margin] themselves unto You.
3.notes: imru l-Elohim mah-nora maasekha (H559, H430, H3372, H4639): the congregation handed its line -- how awesome are Your works -- be-rob uzzekha yekhachashu lekha oyebekha (H7230, H5797, H3584, H341): the margin's 'feigned obedience' -- kachash, to cringe, to lie: enemies submitting because they must, Psalm 18:44's word. Real power produces at least false homage.

4.text: All the earth will bow down to You and make music to You; they will make music to Your name. Selah.
4.amp: All the earth [eretz] shall worship [shachah -- bow down] You, and shall sing [zamar] unto You; they shall sing to Your name [shem]. Selah [selah].
4.notes: kol-ha-aretz yishtachavu lekha (H776, H7812): the whole earth prostrate -- vi-zammeru-lakh, yezammeru shimkha (H2167, H8034): zamar twice, music to You and to Your Name. Verse 3's cringing enemies become verse 4's worshiping earth: the psalm's hope for the nations, Psalm 22:27's arc.

5.text: Come and see the deeds of God -- awesome in His doing toward the children of men.
5.amp: Come [yalak] and see [raah] the works [miphal -- deeds] of God [Elohim]: He is terrible [yare -- awesome] in His doing [alilah] toward the children [ben] of men [adam].
5.notes: lekhu u-reu miphalot Elohim (H3212, H7200, H4659, H430): COME AND SEE -- the invitation Philip gives Nathanael (cf. John 1:46) -- nora alilah al-bene adam (H3372, H5949, H1121, H120): awesome in His dealings with the sons of Adam. The evidence is public; the psalm conducts a tour.

6.text: He turned the sea into dry land; they crossed the river on foot -- there we rejoiced in Him.
6.amp: He turned [haphak] the sea [yam] into dry [yabbashah] land: they went [abar] through the flood [nahar -- river] on foot [regel]: there did we rejoice [samach] in Him.
6.notes: haphakh yam le-yabbashah (H2015, H3220, H3004): the sea turned to dry ground -- Exodus 14 -- ba-nahar yaabru be-ragel (H5104, H5674, H7272): the river crossed on foot -- Joshua 3. sham nismechah-bo (H8055): THERE let us rejoice in Him -- the present congregation putting itself on the far bank of both crossings, as Psalm 114 does.

7.text: He rules by His might forever; His eyes keep watch over the nations. Let the rebels not lift themselves up. Selah.
7.amp: He rules [mashal] by His power [geburah] for ever [olam]; His eyes [ayin] behold [tsaphah -- keep watch] the nations [goy]: let not the rebellious [sarar -- the stubborn] exalt [rum] themselves. Selah [selah].
7.notes: moshel bi-geburato olam (H4910, H1369, H5769): ruling by His might forever -- enav ba-goyim titspenah (H5869, H1471, H6822): His eyes on watch over the nations, the watchman-verb of Psalm 5:3 -- ha-sorerim al-yarumu lamo (H5637, H7311): let the stubborn not raise themselves. The Red Sea's God still has the nations under surveillance.

8.text: O you peoples, bless our God; let the sound of His praise ring out and be heard --
8.amp: O bless [barak] our God [Elohim], ye people [am], and make the voice [qol] of His praise [tehillah] to be heard [shama]:
8.notes: barekhu ammim Elohenu (H1288, H5971, H430): PEOPLES, plural, told to bless OUR God -- ve-hashmiu qol tehillato (H8085, H6963, H8416): make the sound of His praise audible. The nations are invited into Israel's own doxology.

9.text: the One who keeps our soul among the living and does not let our foot slip.
9.amp: Which holds ['putteth', sum, the KJV margin] our soul [nephesh] in life [chay], and suffers [natan -- allows] not our feet [regel] to be moved [mot -- slip].
9.notes: ha-sam naphshenu ba-chayyim (H7760, H5315, H2416): the margin's 'putteth' -- He SET our soul among the living, placed it there -- ve-lo-natan la-mot raglenu (H5414, H4132, H7272): and did not give our foot over to slipping. Survival and footing, the two things Psalm 121 also credits to the Keeper.

10.text: For You tested us, O God; You refined us as silver is refined.
10.amp: For You, O God [Elohim], have proved [bachan -- tested, assayed] us: You have tried [tsaraph -- refined, smelted] us, as silver [keseph] is tried [tsaraph].
10.notes: ki-bechantanu Elohim (H974, H430): You assayed us -- tseraphtanu ki-tseroph-kaseph (H6884, H3701): refined us the way silver is refined -- in a crucible, by heat, with the dross skimmed. The nation's suffering read as smelting, not punishment (cf. Malachi 3:3; 1 Peter 1:7).

11.text: You brought us into the net; You laid a heavy load on our hips.
11.amp: You brought [bo] us into the net [metsudah -- the hunter's net, the prison]; You laid [sum] affliction [muaqah -- pressure, affliction] upon our loins [mothen -- hips].
11.notes: habetanu ba-metsudah (H935, H4686): into the metsudah -- the hunter's net, or the stronghold used as a prison; the WEB has 'prison' -- samta muaqah be-motnenu (H7760, H4157, H4975): a crushing weight set on the loins, where a load is carried. God the trapper, God the taskmaster: the psalm does not flinch from making Him the agent.

12.text: You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water -- and You brought us out into a place of overflowing abundance.
12.amp: You have caused men [enosh -- frail mortals] to ride [rakab] over our heads [rosh]; we went [bo] through fire [esh] and through water [mayim]: but You brought us out [yatsa] into a wealthy ['moist', revayah -- saturation, overflow, the KJV margin] place.
12.notes: hirkabta enosh le-roshenu (H7392, H582, H7218): mere mortals riding over our heads -- the conquered as a road -- banu ba-esh u-ba-mayim (H935, H784, H4325): through fire and water, the two elements that kill -- va-totsienu la-revayah (H3318, H7310): and You brought us out to revayah, the margin's 'moist': the saturated place, Psalm 23:5's overflowing cup. Isaiah 43:2 makes the fire-and-water passage a promise.

13.text: I will enter Your house with whole burnt offerings; I will pay my vows to You --
13.amp: I will go [bo] into Your house [bayith] with burnt offerings [olah -- whole burnt offerings]: I will pay [shalam -- make good] You my vows [neder],
13.notes: abo betekha be-olot (H935, H1004, H5930): the psalm narrows from 'we' to 'I' -- one man entering the house with whole burnt offerings -- ashallem lekha nedarai (H7999, H5088): to pay the vows, Psalm 116:14's discipline. National deliverance, personal bill.

14.text: the vows my lips let out and my mouth spoke when I was in distress.
14.amp: Which my lips [saphah] have uttered ['opened', patsah, the KJV margin], and my mouth [peh] has spoken [dabar], when I was in trouble [tsar -- the tight place].
14.notes: asher-patsu sephatai (H6475, H8193): the margin's 'opened' -- vows that broke out of the lips -- ve-dibber-pi ba-tsar-li (H1696, H6310, H6862): my mouth spoke in the narrows. Promises made in a tight place are collected in a wide one; the psalmist intends to keep his.

15.text: I will offer up to You burnt offerings of fattened animals, with the smoke of rams; I will prepare bulls with goats. Selah.
15.amp: I will offer [alah -- send up] unto You burnt sacrifices [olah] of fatlings ['marrow', meach -- fat beasts, the KJV margin], with the incense [qetoreth -- the smoke] of rams [ayil]; I will offer [asah -- prepare] bullocks [baqar] with goats [attud -- he-goats]. Selah [selah].
15.notes: olot mechim aaleh-lakh (H5930, H4220, H5927): the margin's 'marrow' -- fatlings, the best-fed animals -- im-qetoret elim (H7004, H352): with the smoke of rams; eeseh baqar im-attudim (H6213, H1241, H6260): bulls with he-goats. An extravagant bill paid in full: the size of the offering measures the size of the rescue.

16.text: Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will recount what He has done for my soul.
16.amp: Come [yalak] and hear [shama], all ye that fear [yare] God [Elohim], and I will declare [saphar -- recount] what He has done [asah] for my soul [nephesh].
16.notes: lekhu-shimu (H3212, H8085): verse 5 said 'come and see'; now 'come and HEAR' -- kol-yire Elohim (H3373, H430), all God-fearers -- va-asapperah asher asah le-naphshi (H5608, H6213, H5315): I will recount what He did for MY soul. From the exodus to one man's testimony in eleven verses; the congregation's history and the individual's are the same story.

17.text: To Him I cried with my mouth, and high praise was under my tongue.
17.amp: I cried [qara] unto Him with my mouth [peh], and He was extolled [rum -- lifted high; romam, high praise] with ['under', tachath] my tongue [lashon].
17.notes: elav pi-qarati (H6310, H7121): with my mouth I called -- ve-romam tachat leshoni (H7311, H7318, H8478, H3956): and exaltation was UNDER my tongue -- ready, held there like food, before the answer came. Praise stored under the tongue during the crying: the mouth calling and the tongue already preparing to thank.

18.text: If I had looked with favor on iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
18.amp: If I regard [raah -- look on with regard, cherish] iniquity [aven] in my heart [leb], the Lord [Adonai] will not hear [shama] me:
18.notes: aven im-raiti be-libbi (H205, H7200, H3820): if I had SEEN iniquity in my heart -- looked at it with regard, kept it in view, cherished it -- lo yishma Adonai (H8085, H136): the Lord would not have heard. The verse that has sent more praying people back to examine their own hearts than almost any other, and rightly: not sinlessness, but a heart that is not harboring (cf. Isaiah 59:2; James 4:3).

19.text: But God has in fact heard; He has paid attention to the sound of my prayer.
19.amp: But verily [aken -- surely, in fact] God [Elohim] has heard [shama] me; He has attended [qashab -- listened intently] to the voice [qol] of my prayer [tephillah].
19.notes: akhen shama Elohim (H403, H8085, H430): but SURELY God heard -- aken is the word of a conclusion reached against doubt -- hiqshib be-qol tephillati (H7181, H6963, H8605): He attended to the voice of my prayer. The heard prayer proves, by verse 18's logic, that the heart was not harboring; the answer is the assurance.

20.text: Blessed be God, who has not turned my prayer away, nor His covenant love from me.
20.amp: Blessed [barak] be God [Elohim], which has not turned away [sur] my prayer [tephillah], nor His mercy [chesed -- covenant love] from me.
20.notes: barukh Elohim asher lo-hesir tephillati ve-chasdo me-itti (H1288, H430, H5493, H8605, H2617): blessed be God, who did not turn aside my prayer -- OR His covenant love -- from me: the two are named together because they arrive together. A psalm that opened with all the earth shouting ends with one man blessing God for one answered prayer, and the two ends are the same praise.
